clue.text: Gold box artist makes musicians

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold
a chest is a large box
RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: A painter with a golden box somehow wins over a band of players.
explanation.definitionFit: A large ensemble of instrumental players performing together is an orchestra.

clue.text: Lawsuit about university sale

indicators.note: about means going round, so the lawsuit word wraps the university letter

parts.note: an action is a case brought in a court

explanation.surface: A legal case concerning a college's disposal of property.
explanation.definitionFit: A public sale where goods go to the highest bidder is an auction.

clue.text: Stubborn doctor returned about one and was in charge

indicators.note: about means the turned doctor goes round the letter for one
returned means the doctor's letters are read backwards

parts.note: GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor
I is the Roman numeral for one
to have headed something is to have led it

explanation.surface: An obstinate physician came back around and took control.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obstinately refusing to change their mind is called pig-headed, an idiom.

clue.text: Cast out worthless type about to produce hopeless situation

indicators.note: about means the worthless type goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible, worthless person

indicators.note: out signals the letters of cast are put out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A rotten character has been thrown out, leaving a situation beyond saving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast out' reads as one verb, expelled, but 'out' is the anagram signal, making STCA for 'about' to put inside the worthless type.
explanation.definitionFit: A cause or venture with no chance of success is an idiom for a hopeless situation.

clue.text: I left with fast pulse

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: Someone went off leaving a quick beat in the wrist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' looks like a heartbeat and 'fast' like speed, but pulses are edible seeds and the fast is Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are the edible seeds of legumes, and the lentil is one such seed.

clue.text: Worn out by the boss!

parts.note: read as a garment worn in public by whoever is in charge, recalling the idiom about the dominant partner in a household

explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn out' suggests exhausted, but it means worn outdoors; the person in charge of a household is said to wear these.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'wear the trousers' means to be the one in control, so the boss wears legwear.

clue.text: A short, talkative cook's fruit

indicators.note: short means the talkative word loses its final letter

parts.note: vocal means outspoken or talkative
to do food is to cook it, as in a well-done steak; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A curt, chatty chef's piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the last letter from VOCAL to leave VOCA.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is a pear-shaped tropical fruit with a large stone.

clue.text: Frank takes some cornflakes in cereal bowl

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A man called Frank helps himself to a share of breakfast cereal from the bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is an adjective meaning honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank and genuine both describe someone open and honest in what they say.

clue.text: Debauched old man swallows a can every day

indicators.note: swallows means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a roue is a dissolute, debauched man, usually older
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A dissolute old fellow downs a can daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Something routine is everyday, done habitually as a matter of course.

clue.text: Device for directing traffic around fallen tree trunk in city

indicators.note: around means the traffic device encloses the fallen trunk

parts.note: a cone is a plastic marker used to direct traffic
a log is a felled section of tree trunk

explanation.surface: A bollard placed round a toppled trunk in a town's street.
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne is a German city on the Rhine, also famous for its scent.

clue.text: Chat about the shimmering axe

indicators.note: about means the letters of chat are turned around into another order
shimmering suggests a wavering, unsettled image, so the letters of the are moved

explanation.surface: Gossip about the gleaming chopper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CHAT to HATC and 'shimmering' rearranges THE to HET.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchet is a small short-handled axe.

clue.text: Curry, say, fish in boiled rice

indicators.note: in means the fish sits inside the reworked rice
boiled suggests the rice is cooked and broken up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a skate is a flat fish of the ray family

explanation.surface: A curry, for example, with fish cooked in rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curry' sits first so its capital hides the person: John Curry, Britain's 1976 Olympic figure-skating champion. 'boiled' makes ICER, which goes round the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: John Curry won Olympic gold in figure skating, so he is an example of one who glides on blades.

clue.text: Businessman and continental headdress

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
Ron is a man's name
et is the French, so continental, word for and

explanation.surface: A trader and a European with an ornamental hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Businessman' must be split in two for the wordplay, a liberty some solvers dislike; 'continental' means the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown worn by nobles, a type of headdress.

clue.text: Could you get opal with a sou here? No, but you might if it were real!

definitions.text: Could you get opal with a sou here? No, but you might if it were real!

indicators.note: asks whether these letters could be got by rearranging, so the gem and coin are mixed together

explanation.surface: A traveller wonders whether a gem could be bought for a small coin in a Brazilian city.
explanation.walkthrough: OPAL plus A SOU rearranges to the city; the sou is French, but Brazil's currency is the real, hence the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Sao Paulo is Brazil's largest city, where the currency is the real.

clue.text: Island tracks broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is heard spoken aloud

parts.note: roads are tracks or routes

explanation.surface: An island's routes are on the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean, the largest of the Dodecanese.

clue.text: Omplaint about pie that is rotten

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Omplaint about pie that is rotten': the definition word is garbled, 'Complaint' with its C lost (the Times for the Times blog confirms the online typo); no form here corrects a definition word. Wordplay is an anagram of PIE THAT IS ('rotten').
annotationWithheld.clue: Omplaint about pie that is rotten

clue.text: Any dessert could make you inactive

indicators.note: could make means the letters of the words can be refashioned into another word

parts.note: the words as printed have one S too many; read as 'Any desert', their letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A warning that any pudding will make you sluggish.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the fodder has one S too many: 'dessert' should be 'desert' for the anagram ('could make') to give the nine letters exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedentary lifestyle involves much sitting and little exercise, so it is inactive.

clue.text: In Gaelic language, "nod" strangely means "support"

indicators.note: In means the scrambled nod goes inside the Gaelic language

parts.note: Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic

indicators.note: strangely means the letters of nod are oddly arranged

explanation.surface: A remark on how a nod is translated in Gaelic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns NOD into NDO, which goes 'In' ERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a candidate or plan is to back or approve of it.

clue.text: Penultimate event has a European riding a pig

indicators.note: penultimate means second to last, so the next-to-final letter of event is taken

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
riding means on, as a rider is on a horse

explanation.surface: The second-last race features a European on a pig's back.
explanation.walkthrough: The pig is Napoleon, the ruling boar in Orwell's Animal Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orwell's Animal Farm the tyrant who seizes power is a boar of that name.

clue.text: A jolly girl's fleet

parts.note: a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM
Ada is a girl's name; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A cheerful young woman owns a flotilla.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective but is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, as in the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Eggs sound expensive — how beastly is this!

parts.note: roe is the mass of eggs in a fish

indicators.note: sound means the word is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: dear means costly or expensive

explanation.surface: A diner complains that fish eggs seem pricey.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the exclamation: the answer is a beast, a small European deer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small deer of Europe and Asia, an animal or beast.

clue.text: Being upset, dad fibbed about first punishment administered

indicators.note: about means these pieces surround the opening letter of punishment
being upset means dad's letters are turned over, read backwards

parts.note: Pa is a familiar word for dad
to fib is to lie

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of punishment is used

explanation.surface: Upset, a father lied about the first punishment handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being upset' turns PA into AP; AP and LIED go 'about' P.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy or penalty that is applied has been administered or put into effect.

clue.text: Mum cuddles a man — making him go this colour

indicators.note: cuddles means mum's letters wrap round the following pieces

parts.note: Ma is a word for mum
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A mother hugs a man until he blushes deeply.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a purplish-red shade, the hue a man might go when embarrassed.

clue.text: Caper spiced up dace with peas

indicators.note: spiced up means the dish is livened up, so the letters of dace and peas are mixed

explanation.surface: A recipe combining a small fish with peas and spices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caper' looks like the pickled bud, apt to a recipe, but it is a frolic; dace is a small freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a daring or mischievous adventure, a prank or escapade.

clue.text: In Munich, gentleman cracks open extremely sickly drink

indicators.note: cracks open means the German gentleman breaks in between the letters taken
extremely means only the outer letters of sickly are used

parts.note: Herr is German for gentleman or Mr

explanation.surface: A German gentleman opens a bottle of a sweet drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'sickly', S and Y, and HERR goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from southern Spain, a kind of drink.

clue.text: Poor pet housed in part of America

indicators.note: poor suggests something in a sorry, disordered state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A neglected animal sheltered in an American region.
explanation.definitionFit: The southeastern states of the USA, such as Alabama and Mississippi, are a region of America.

clue.text: Distinguished what belongs to me in hospital department

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the hospital department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
mine means what belongs to me

explanation.surface: A notable man claims his place in a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent and distinguished both mean famous and respected in a field.

clue.text: Render notes on organ

parts.note: D and E are two musical notes
the liver is a bodily organ

explanation.surface: A musician plays notes on an organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests music, as does 'notes', but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To render a service or verdict is to give it over, to hand it in.

clue.text: One in list of names is a reveller

indicators.note: in means the letter for one goes inside the list of names

parts.note: a roster is a list of names on a rota
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A person on the duty list turns out to be a party-goer.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic noun names a noisy merrymaker, one who carouses.

clue.text: Wisely change for lent? Dry up!

indicators.note: change means the letters of the words are swapped into a new order

explanation.surface: A suggestion to give up drink for Lent, with a curt order to stop talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with prudence means behaving sensibly and with good judgement, so wisely.
